text.p: A 30-km (19-mile) stretch of motorway south of Sydney was closed for more than eight hours on Monday after nine trucks and two cars were involved in two separate accidents, police said.
Ten people were injured, two seriously, in the early morning collisions on the F-5 freeway near Mittagong, about 100 kms (60 miles) south of Sydney, a police spokesman said.
Police blamed the accidents on foggy conditions and lingering smoke from a controlled burn-off of bushland nearby.
Burn-offs are carried out to reduce the risk of bush fires during the hot summer season.
"Even with warning lights, vision was down to only about 20 feet (six metres)," the spokesman said.
Seven semi-trailers and a car collided in an accident on the northbound side of the freeway, while two trucks and a car collided on the opposite side of the road, police said.
